title: Who Ate The Halloween Candy
trend: Instagram Reels / TikTok 'Netflix documentary' chair-sit parody (narrating an ordinary event with total gravity over dramatic music; on SocialBee's and AniJam's 2026 trend lists) applied to the US pre-Halloween moment of eating the trick-or-treat candy you bought too early (Halloween in eleven days)

lines.text: On October first, I bought four bags of Halloween candy.
Early. To get the good kind.
Today is October twentieth. There is one bag left.
Halloween is in eleven days. Someone in this house is a monster.
It is spooky season. Everyone is a monster.
Hank. Please sit in the chair.
Okay. For the record, I have eaten zero pieces of candy.
He has eaten forty one fun size bars.
Fun size is not a piece. Fun size is a feeling.
A feeling with chocolate on your hoodie.
Every night at eleven, he sneaks downstairs in socks.
Then he eats the evidence and folds every wrapper into a tiny square.
Where are the tiny squares, Hank?
In my other socks.
Next witness. The candy bowl.
I am a plastic pumpkin. I have held Halloween candy since nineteen ninety eight.
I have held raisins. Nobody wants the raisins. They will outlive us all.
Everyone in this house. And one person who does not live in this house.
Evening.
Earl. I live under your deck. I pay rent in eye contact.
There has been a raccoon under the deck?
Since the barbecue. You called me a big cat.
Earl. Have you been eating our Halloween candy?
Ma'am, I eat garbage. I have standards. Low ones.
And lately your garbage has been full of tiny folded squares.
Those were in my socks!
Your sock was in the garbage, sir. The left one.
I wear it now. As a scarf. It is very warm.
So it was Hank. Case closed.
Hank is a small fish, ma'am.
Some wrappers were not folded. Only peanut butter cups.
Who in this house only eats the peanut butter ones?
Gwen.
I was testing them. For quality. For the children.
You tested thirty two of them.
Quality is a journey.
You put me in the documentary chair!
Every documentary needs a red herring. You were in a red hoodie.
This is my only hoodie!
Okay. Okay. Here is the real truth.
There were never four bags. There were eight. I hid four of them in the dryer.
Then we are fine! We are totally fine!
The dryer has been running since Saturday.
That was me. I washed my hoodie. Because of the feeling.
So that is the smell. The whole street smells like warm caramel.
Four bags of candy. Now one very big candy. Shaped like a dryer.
So. One bag. Eleven days. And a dryer full of fudge.
New plan. We give out the raisins.
No.
Can I keep the sock?
Keep the sock, Earl.
This has been a documentary. Nobody learned anything.
Hank. Is that a peanut butter cup in your hand?
It is fun size. It does not count.
